column1: A stored procedure compiles for the target platform. What does a unit test tell you that the build cannot?
column2:
An individual procedure or function produces the expected behavior for known inputs.
A build can accept a procedure that returns the wrong total. A unit test supplies known inputs and compares the output or resulting state with what the individual object is meant to produce.
Review source

column1: What does a database integration test check when a procedure writes a row and fires a trigger?
column2:
A workflow involving multiple database objects or application operations working together.
An integration test tests the connection between components. For example, call the order procedure and check that its trigger creates the expected history row. Either object can work by itself while the workflow fails.
Review source

column1: Which Visual Studio tooling provides the SQL Server Unit Test Designer?
column2:
SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT).
SQL Server Data Tools (SSDT) provides the designer in Visual Studio. A test runs T-SQL against a test database and applies conditions to the result. It checks behavior that a project build cannot prove.
Review source

column1: Which SSDT test condition verifies the number of rows returned by a query?
column2:
Row Count.
Row Count checks how many rows the selected result set contains. For example, a lookup query can be required to return one row. This is different from checking how many rows an UPDATE modified.
Review source

column1: Which SSDT test condition compares one returned cell with an expected value?
column2:
Scalar Value.
Scalar Value checks one cell at a specified row and column. For example, test that the first row's total equals 42. Use Row Count if the number of returned rows is what matters.
Review source

column1: Which SSDT condition checks returned column names and types rather than row values?
column2:
Expected Schema.
Expected Schema checks the structure returned by the query. A column with a new name or type can fail this condition even if the data looks the same. It does not compare the returned values.
Review source

column1: When you give a procedure invalid input, what must a negative test verify?
column2:
Invalid inputs produce the intended failure instead of silent success.
A negative test gives the database input it must reject. For example, cancel an order that already shipped and require the expected SQL error. Any unrelated error does not necessarily prove the rule worked.
Review source

column1: Where must database unit and integration tests run to protect production?
column2:
In an isolated test database, separate from production.
Both test types execute SQL and can write rows, change state, or fail before cleanup. Use a separate test database so those effects cannot alter production data or disrupt its workload.
Review source

column1: Why reset test data to a known state before each database test run?
column2:
Results must depend on test inputs, not leftover data from earlier runs.
Starting with the same test data makes repeated outcomes comparable. Rows left by a previous test can hide a defect or cause a false failure. A schema deployment alone need not reset existing rows.
Review source

column1: Which SSDT setting deploys the current schema to the test database before tests run?
column2:
Automatically deploy the database project before running tests.
Automatic deployment publishes the project to the configured test database before the tests run. This helps the tests exercise the current schema. Make sure that the destination is the intended test database.
Review source

column1: What test result must a CI/CD pipeline require before it promotes a DACPAC to staging or production?
column2:
Require a successful test stage before downstream deployment.
Make downstream deployment depend on a passing test stage. Build the artifact and test it against a dedicated database first. A failed test then prevents that run from promoting the artifact.
Review source

column1: What placeholder condition must you remove after adding a real check to an SSDT test?
column2:
Inconclusive.
Inconclusive is a placeholder for a test without meaningful verification. It always reports inconclusive. Remove it once a real condition can distinguish correct behavior from a failure.
Review source

column1: Which Azure Pipelines task runs compiled tests on the Visual Studio test platform?
column2:
VSTest@3.
VSTest@3 discovers tests in compiled assemblies through supported adapters. It is for the Visual Studio test platform, not Microsoft.Testing.Platform. Build the test assemblies before asking the task to run them.
Review source
